1.1 In this Agreement, unless the context otherwise requires:

“Business Day” means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday, or public holiday in Nigeria.

“Contract Price” means the prices set out in Schedule 1, as adjusted in accordance with Clause 8.

“Delivery Order” means a written order placed by the Buyer via email or the Supplier’s online ordering portal, specifying the Products, quantities, and requested delivery date.

“Force Majeure” means any event beyond the reasonable control of a Party, including but not limited to acts of God, war, terrorism, strike, lockout, fire, flood, epidemic, governmental action, or breakdown of transportation infrastructure.

“Products” means the food items and related supplies listed in Schedule 1, together with any substitutes or replacements agreed in writing under Clause 7.

“Quality Standards” means the specifications set out in Schedule 2, including freshness, packaging, and temperature requirements.

“Specification” means, in relation to any Product, the description, quality, grade, packaging, and labelling requirements set out in Schedule 2.

1.2 Clause headings are for convenience only and do not affect interpretation. Words importing the singular include the plural and vice versa. References to “writing” include email.

2. TERM

2.1 This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and, unless terminated earlier in accordance with Clause 12, shall continue for an initial term of 12 months (the “Initial Term”).

2.2 Upon expiry of the Initial Term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive periods of 12 months (each a “Renewal Term”), unless either Party gives the other not less than 60 days’ written notice of non-renewal prior to the expiry of the then-current term.

2.3 The Supply Agreement 2024-01 specifies an initial_term_months of 12 months. Record status: current.

3. SUPPLY OF PRODUCTS

3.1 The Supplier shall supply the Products to the Buyer in accordance with the terms of this Agreement, each Delivery Order, and the Quality Standards.

3.2 The Buyer shall place Delivery Orders at least 48 hours before the requested delivery date, except for emergency orders which may be placed with shorter notice if the Supplier agrees.

3.3 The Supplier shall use reasonable endeavours to deliver the full quantity ordered under each Delivery Order. If the Supplier anticipates a shortfall, it shall notify the Buyer as soon as reasonably practicable and propose a substitute Product of equivalent or better quality, subject to Clause 7.

3.4 All Products shall be delivered in clean, food-grade packaging bearing the Product name, batch number, and expiry date where applicable.

4. DELIVERY

4.1 Deliveries shall be made to the Buyer’s premises at Plot 14B, Admiralty Way, Lekki Phase 1, Lagos, or to such other location as the Buyer may specify in a Delivery Order.

4.2 Unless otherwise agreed in writing, deliveries shall be made on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays between 7:00 a.m. and 11:00 a.m. (WAT). The Supplier shall provide the Buyer with the vehicle registration number and driver contact details not later than one hour before the estimated arrival.

4.3 Risk in the Products shall pass to the Buyer upon delivery and signing of the delivery note. Title in the Products shall pass to the Buyer upon full payment for the relevant Delivery Order.

5. QUALITY AND INSPECTION

5.1 The Supplier warrants that all Products shall:
6. PRICES AND PAYMENT

6.1 The prices for the Products shall be as set out in the Price Schedule attached as Schedule 1 to this Agreement, as the same may be varied from time to time in accordance with this Clause 6.

6.2 Prices shall be quoted in Nigerian Naira (₦) and shall be exclusive of Value Added Tax (VAT), which shall be added at the applicable rate.

6.3 The prices set out in Schedule 1 shall remain firm and fixed for the first 6 months of the Initial Term, commencing on the Effective Date.

6.4 Price Escalation:

(a) Subject to Clause 6.4(b), with effect from the first day of the seventh (7th) month of the Initial Term, and thereafter on each anniversary of the Effective Date during any Renewal Term, the prices set out in Schedule 1 shall be adjusted by an amount not exceeding 5% per annum (the “Annual Adjustment”).

(b) The Supply Agreement 2024-01 includes a price_escalation_clause of 5% annual increase based on NBS food inflation index. Record status: current. The Annual Adjustment shall be calculated by reference to the percentage change in the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) Food Price Index (or any successor index) published for the most recent available month prior to the adjustment date, compared with the corresponding month in the preceding year.

(c) The resulting adjusted price shall be the lower of: (i) the previous price increased by 5%; or (ii) the previous price increased by the percentage change in the NBS Food Price Index. For the avoidance of doubt, the Annual Adjustment shall not exceed 5% in any 12-month period.

(d) The Supplier shall notify the Buyer in writing of any adjustment to prices under this Clause 6.4 not less than 14 days before the adjustment takes effect, and shall provide reasonable supporting documentation evidencing the NBS Food Price Index figures used.

(e) If the NBS Food Price Index is discontinued or its methodology is materially changed, the Parties shall negotiate in good faith to agree an alternative index or methodology.

6.5 No other price increases shall apply during the term of this Agreement, save as expressly provided in this Clause 6.

6.6 Invoicing:

(a) The Supplier shall issue a single consolidated invoice for each Delivery Order, which shall be delivered to the Buyer by email to accounts@lagoonbites.ng and by hard copy with the delivery note.

(b) Each invoice shall state the Delivery Order number, the date of delivery, itemised quantities and unit prices for each Product, the applicable VAT, the total amount due, and the payment terms as set out in Clause 6.7.

(c) The Supplier shall issue a credit note in respect of any Products rejected under Clause 5 or returned under Clause 8, and shall set off such credit against the next invoice issued to the Buyer.

6.7 Payment Terms:

(a) The Buyer shall pay each invoice within 30 days of the date of the invoice, by direct bank transfer to the Supplier’s nominated account, details of which are set out in Schedule 2.

(b) Payment shall be made in Nigerian Naira. The Buyer shall notify the Supplier by email of the reference number of each transfer not later than one business day after making payment.

(c) If the Buyer disputes any part of an invoice, it shall notify the Supplier in writing within 10 business days of receipt of the invoice, specifying the disputed items and the reasons for the dispute. The undisputed portion of the invoice shall be paid in accordance with Clause 6.7(a).
(a) If the Supplier delivers less than the quantity of any Product specified in a Delivery Order, the shortfall shall be noted on the delivery note and the Supplier shall deliver the shortfall quantity at the next scheduled delivery, unless the Buyer agrees otherwise in writing.

(b) If the Supplier delivers more than the quantity of any Product specified in a Delivery Order, the Buyer may reject the excess quantity at the point of delivery, and the Supplier shall arrange for its collection at the Supplier’s cost. The Buyer shall not be obliged to pay for any excess quantity delivered without its prior written consent.

**7.4 Delivery Delays**

(a) If the Supplier anticipates that a delivery will be delayed by more than one (1) hour beyond the scheduled arrival window, it shall notify the Buyer by telephone and email immediately upon becoming aware of the delay, stating the revised estimated time of arrival and the reason for the delay.

(b) Subject to Clause 12 (Force Majeure), if the Supplier fails to deliver any Products on the scheduled delivery date, the Buyer shall be entitled, without prejudice to its other rights and remedies, to:

(i) procure the affected Products from an alternative supplier and charge the Supplier any additional costs reasonably incurred; and/or

(ii) claim liquidated damages in accordance with Clause 7.5.

**7.5 Liquidated Damages for Late Delivery**

(a) If the Supplier fails to deliver all or part of a Delivery Order on the scheduled delivery date, the Supplier shall pay to the Buyer liquidated damages of 0.5% of the value of the undelivered Products for each complete day of delay, up to a maximum of 10% of the value of the undelivered Products.

(b) The Parties agree that the liquidated damages set out in this Clause 7.5 are a genuine pre-estimate of the loss likely to be suffered by the Buyer as a result of late delivery and are not a penalty.

(a) The Supplier may set a credit limit for the Buyer, which shall be reviewed quarterly. The initial credit limit is ₦2,500,000 (Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Naira).
